text: Write a program showing that `static` methods are hidden rather than overridden. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: static class A { static String s() { return "A.static"; } String who() { return "A"; } }
explanation: Verified: `A.static` then `B`. A `static` method belongs to the class, so there is nothing to dispatch on and the declared type decides — the same rule as overloading. Calling a static method through a reference is legal and misleading, which is why most tools warn about it and why writing `A.s()` makes the situation impossible to misread.
